request: Use REAL-UI to make a FULL REDESIGN of this bilingual browser gaming product. Preserve its real requirements, capabilities, workflows, routes, data, logic, and recognizable playfulness. Do not use the existing presentation as the new composition. Implement and validate the result in a browser.

product.purpose: Let Arabic- and English-speaking casual players enter a browser game immediately, resume local progress, and discover another short game without an account.
primary_tasks: check today's challenge and personal progress
relationships: progress and scores belong to this device
seo_requirements: crawlable game names and category links

presentation_before.navigation_model: top brand links with search plus duplicated bottom tabs
presentation_before.density: one large promotional block followed by uniform browse rows
presentation_before.responsive_model: desktop sections stack into the same vertical order on phone
presentation_before.silhouette: split hero -> ad rectangle -> resume cards -> filtered card grid

research.label: PLATFORM RULE
research.finding: Game UI navigation and focus should stay logical, consistent, predictable, and operable with digital input.
research.product_use: The play deck, library switcher, and score view share one predictable focus order; the evidence does not prescribe a hero or grid.

research.label: PLATFORM RULE
research.finding: Content and controls must reflow without two-dimensional page scrolling at the required narrow equivalent.
research.product_use: The desktop play deck becomes phone task tabs rather than a squeezed split hero.

research.label: SOURCE-OBSERVED
research.finding: Browser-game discovery is thumbnail-led and play should be low-friction; genre business models are not scope evidence.
research.product_use: Keep one-step play and media-led selection while excluding unsupported advertising.

user_priorities: see what can be played now
research_findings: reflow should change the interaction model
design_brief.ia_direction: Organize home around the play session: resume/start, active game context, library switching, then progress and challenge history.
design_brief.navigation_direction: Use a compact task switcher for Play, Library, Challenge, and Scores; search lives in the library rather than competing in the global masthead.
design_brief.content_representation: A persistent play deck carries the current game; a dense ranked library list replaces the poster grid; progress and daily state become contextual ledgers.
design_brief.interaction_direction: Resume and quick-switch are one action; keyboard focus follows the visible deck-to-library order; touch uses labeled task tabs.
responsive_priorities: turn the side library into a dedicated task view
structures_to_preserve: recognized brand wordmark and playful direct copy
structures_to_change: merge resume into the play deck
replace uniform grid with library explorer

decisions.decision: Make the active play session the home composition anchor.
decisions.evidence: resume/play are the top-frequency tasks in the extracted product
decisions.product_reason: players arrive to play, not consume a promotion

decisions.decision: Replace the uniform card catalog with a searchable ranked library list.
decisions.evidence: 16 known items, categories, personal recency, and pointer/keyboard switching
decisions.product_reason: the list exposes progress and recent state without duplicating card chrome

decisions.evidence: no user or product requirement authorizes ads; prior ad scope was inferred
decisions.product_reason: genre prevalence cannot create a business model

scope_ledger.reason: future plan only; v1 is local

proposed_structure.navigation_model: task switcher for play/library/challenge/scores with localized language control
proposed_structure.density: one high-focus play surface with dense supporting library and ledgers
proposed_structure.responsive_model: desktop play deck plus library; phone labeled task tabs with play first and library as its own view
proposed_structure.silhouette: session dock -> asymmetric play workspace -> compact return ledgers

structural_decisions.before: top links plus duplicated bottom tabs
structural_decisions.evidence: top tasks and XAG navigation consistency
structural_decisions.product_reason: makes play modes explicit without duplicated hierarchy

structural_decisions.after: session, play, library, challenge, score zones
structural_decisions.product_reason: each region maps to an existing capability

structural_decisions.after: resume/play before switching and return loops

structural_decisions.product_reason: groups by player intent rather than old sections
attention concentrates on playing while choices stay compact
mobile is not a squeezed desktop play workspace
the structure expresses the product rather than a portal template
